title: POC Weekly Sync - Rollout / Go-Live Planning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on finalizing the canary cutover plan and runbook for production rollout. SE walked through proposed traffic split, monitoring dashboards, and fallback logic. Customer raised SSO/KMS questions and asked for a short load benchmark for 10% canary. Next steps include benchmark results, updated runbook link, and scheduling a dry-run cutover.
next_steps: Marcus to run 10% canary benchmark and share results by 2026-11-11
Lena to send pricing summary and canary SLA options by 2026-11-06
Sam to review runbook and confirm security notes by 2026-11-09
Schedule dry-run cutover (2-hour window) week of 2026-11-16
action_items: Marcus Diaz - run canary benchmark (10% traffic) and upload results to shared spreadsheet - due 2026-11-11
Lena Park - send pricing breakdown and SLA options for dedicated capacity - due 2026-11-06
Sam Torres (Atlas) - review runbook and confirm KMS/SSO requirements - due 2026-11-09
Priya Nair - create post-mortem template and incident runbook section - due 2026-11-13
transcript:
[00:00:05] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call before we jump in—Lena from Redwood, Marcus SE, Priya on CSM side. Jared, Maya, Evan, Nora — you there?
[00:00:15] Jared Kim: Yep, Jared here. Thanks.
[00:00:18] Maya Singh: Maya here.
[00:00:20] Evan Cole: Evan.
[00:00:22] Nora Patel: Nora.
[00:00:24] Sam Torres: Sam from security.
[00:00:27] Lena Park: Great. Agenda is the rollout / go-live plan: cutover approach, canary vs A/B, monitoring and runbooks, and outstanding security items. We'll keep this to 45 minutes. Marcus will walk through the canary flow.
[00:00:40] Marcus Diaz: Thanks. So high level — propose 3-phase cutover: first a 10% canary for 72 hours with synthetic traffic and real traffic mix, second a 50% ramp for 24 hours, final cutover at 100% with a 2-hour dry-run window. For canary we want to run the same prompt sets used in the POC, plus a small spike test. The canary will be routed to Redwood Dedicated nodes with autoscaling disabled for predictability, and fallback to hosted if latency or error rate crosses thresholds.
[00:01:15] Maya Singh: Quick question — why Dedicated for canary? I thought we were planning Redwood Hosted for lower friction.
[00:01:22] Marcus Diaz: Good call — mostly for isolation and predictable perf. We can do 10% on Dedicated and the rest on Hosted for an A/B style run if you'd prefer. Dedicated gives us control over quantization and kernel selection so we can guarantee latency SLOs.
[00:01:38] Nora Patel: Is there a cost delta there we should expect during canary?
[00:01:42] Lena Park: Yes there is. I'll send a short pricing breakdown after this call — options with Dedicated reserved for canary and a burst policy. Also a lower-cost path would be to run the canary on a lower-performance Dedicated variant.
[00:01:55] Evan Cole: On the monitoring front, what dashboards will we get? Token-level latency, error rate, per-route breakdown?
[00:02:02] Marcus Diaz: We'll provide Redwood Console dashboards with per-route latency, p50/p95/p99, tokens per second, and a separate canary panel. We'll also push logs to your Splunk/Datadog endpoint and ship trace spans. Note: our exporter sometimes labels KV cache as "K V cash" in auto-transcripts, sorry for the weirdness.
[00:02:20] Sam Torres: On security — we need confirmation on KMS integration, SAML SSO, and audit log retention for 365 days.
[00:02:27] Lena Park: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS and SSO; we'll attach SOC 2 attestations. I'll link the security pack after. Marcus, can you note the audit log path?
[00:02:36] Marcus Diaz: Audit logs will be available in the Private control plane and can be forwarded to your SIEM — retention configurable up to 2 years on request. KMS can be either Cloud KMS or HSM via our integration.
[00:02:47] Maya Singh: For rollbacks — can you summarize the automated fallback?
[00:02:52] Marcus Diaz: Sure — we have policy-based routing: if error rate > 2% or p95 latency > 800ms sustained over 3 minutes, traffic shifts back to last-known-good model variant or the Hosted fallback. We also can pause the canary completely via a kick button in the Console.
[00:03:07] Nora Patel: And what about data residency — we need EU region only for some traffic.
[00:03:12] Lena Park: We can pin region by route; the routing policy will keep EU traffic in the EU region. We'll document that in the runbook.
[00:03:18] Marcus Diaz: Next I want to call out the load test we recommend for the 10% canary. Run a sustained 5-minute ramp to P50 traffic levels and a 30-second spike at 3x to validate autoscaling behavior and OOM safety in the model servers.
[00:03:33] Evan Cole: For autoscaling, you said disabled earlier — are we enabling it for the ramp?
[00:03:36] Marcus Diaz: For the canary phase we suggest autoscaling off to keep the baseline stable. For the 50% ramp we can enable autoscaling with conservative thresholds.
[00:03:45] Jared Kim: I want to be explicit about success criteria — our SLOs are p95 < 600ms for the fast paths and error rate < 1%. If those hold for 48 hours on canary, we'll consider ramping to 50%.
[00:03:58] Maya Singh: Also quality checks — we need to run our eval suite (1000 prompts) and ensure no regression in ROUGE/BLEU-ish metrics and also human spot checks.
[00:04:08] Marcus Diaz: That's in scope — we'll run the POC eval harness and surface any regressions in the Redwood Console QA panel. Note that tokenization differences and quantization can cause small variances; we'll flag anything over your threshold.
[00:04:21] Priya Nair: I've added a section in the runbook for QA gating. I'll link to the deck and shared spreadsheet after the call.
[00:04:28] Nora Patel: On runbooks — can we get a dry-run checklist? Steps for cutover, rollback, and post-cutover validation?
[00:04:34] Marcus Diaz: Absolutely. Our runbook template includes pre-cutover validation (smoke tests, secrets check, KMS connectivity), canary run steps, monitoring thresholds, and rollback procedures. We'll also include run commands and the Synthetic prompt list.
[00:04:47] Jared Kim: Who is the on-call during cutover? We need names and escalation paths.
[00:04:52] Lena Park: For the cutover dry-run, Redwood will have Marcus and one SRE on call; Atlas to provide Evan plus an executive contact. We'll capture escalation matrix in the runbook.
[00:05:00] Sam Torres: Security note — before canary, Sam asks for a brief architecture diagram and confirmation that keys never leave the customer KMS.
[00:05:07] Marcus Diaz: We'll provide an architecture diagram and an HSM flow. Keys are used via envelope encryption; model servers don't hold plaintext keys.
[00:05:15] Maya Singh: A couple of small ops items — metrics cardinality; we don't want noisy high-cardinality tags causing costs.
[00:05:20] Marcus Diaz: Good point — we'll limit per-request tags to route, model, and env. We'll provide a recommended tag set in the dashboard config.
[00:05:28] Nora Patel: What's the plan for canary traffic weighting? Linear ramp?
[00:05:31] Marcus Diaz: For the 10% canary it's a static 10% for 72 hours. If stable, we move to 50% for 24hrs and then to 100%. For a faster path we can do an A/B where we put 10% real users on new model variant and 90% on old, and run side-by-side evaluation. That requires simple client-side split or feature flag.
[00:05:50] Jared Kim: We prefer server-side routing to avoid client changes.
[00:05:53] Marcus Diaz: Server-side routing works fine. We'll implement traffic steering in the control plane.
[00:05:58] Evan Cole: About observability — what alerts are you recommending? Pager for Sev 1 on error spikes, Slack for anomalies, and weekly digest?
[00:06:05] Marcus Diaz: Exactly: Sev1 pager on sustained error > 3% for 5 minutes, Sev2 Slack for p95 breaches for 10 minutes. We'll also push daily summaries and a weekly health digest.
[00:06:14] Maya Singh: Can we get a test harness to run locally for the eval?
[00:06:18] Marcus Diaz: Yes, we'll share a small containerized harness that mirrors the POC prompt set and the eval script.
[00:06:23] Priya Nair: I have a note — we'll include a checklist for IAM, SAML, KMS, and audit logs in the runbook.
[00:06:30] Sam Torres: One more security item — we need to confirm that Redwood's penetration test schedule and if Atlas can request a targeted PT for the private deployment.
[00:06:36] Lena Park: We run annual pentests; we can coordinate a targeted assessment for the Private deployment — Marcus will loop in our security team.
[00:06:44] Marcus Diaz: I'll open a ticket with security and include contact points.
[00:06:47] Nora Patel: About data retention for audit logs — can you set a default retention for 365 but allow longer on request?
[00:06:53] Marcus Diaz: Yes, default 365 days, extendable.
[00:06:57] Jared Kim: Let's talk about the canary benchmark specifics — Marcus you mentioned synthetic tests and POC prompt sets; can you also run 95th percentile latency under TLS termination and tokenization variance included?
[00:07:08] Marcus Diaz: Yes, tests will be run end-to-end including TLS termination, tokenizer round trips, and K V cache warm/cold cycles. We'll include cold start tests for the cache and steady-state token generation.
[00:07:20] Maya Singh: For the evaluation pass/fail criteria — define thresholds: p95 < 600ms, error < 1%, no >5% model-quality regression on evaluation metrics.
[00:07:29] Jared Kim: Agreed.
[00:07:31] Marcus Diaz: Noted. We'll run bench and report p50/p95/p99, error rate, and quality delta.
[00:07:36] Priya Nair: I'll update the runbook doc with those thresholds now and share link.
[00:07:40] Lena Park: Okay next — outage strategy. If canary fails, we want an automated fast rollback plus a manual runbook. Is that clear?
[00:07:47] Marcus Diaz: Yes. Auto rollback to last-known-good for critical thresholds, and manual instructions in the runbook for partial traffic rehealing.
[00:07:55] Evan Cole: What's the expected time to rollback?
[00:07:58] Marcus Diaz: Automated rollback within 30-60 seconds after threshold detected; full customer-safe rollback (including cache priming) in 5-15 minutes depending on model size.
[00:08:07] Nora Patel: Do we need a DB migration or any schema changes?
[00:08:10] Lena Park: No DB changes for this release. It's purely inference path.
[00:08:13] Jared Kim: For compliance — Sam, once you sign off, can we get the security appendix attached to the MSA?
[00:08:19] Sam Torres: Yes, after the architecture and KMS confirmations I'll sign off.
[00:08:23] Marcus Diaz: Quick note — one minor transcription quirk, our auto notes sometimes call "Redwood Dedicated" as "Redwood Dedicate" in speech, ignore that.
[00:08:32] Maya Singh: Anything else on rollout?
[00:08:34] Lena Park: Let's capture the concrete timeline. Proposal: run canary starting 2026-11-18 for 72 hours, benchmark results due by 2026-11-11, dry-run week of 2026-11-16, final cutover after exec sign-off. Does that work?
[00:08:50] Jared Kim: Timeline looks good.
[00:08:52] Nora Patel: Works for product.
[00:08:54] Sam Torres: Security tentative — need to complete architecture review.
[00:08:58] Priya Nair: I'll schedule the dry-run and send calendar invites for the on-call rotations.
[00:09:03] Marcus Diaz: I'll start the benchmark run today and aim to push results to the spreadsheet by next week.
[00:09:09] Lena Park: Great. Quick recap and owners: Marcus runs benchmark, Lena sends pricing, Sam reviews security, Priya builds runbook and dry-run invites. We'll share links after the call — runbook: [link to rollout runbook doc], benchmark sheet: [link to benchmark spreadsheet], security pack: [link to security pack].
[00:09:30] Jared Kim: Thanks all. One last ask — can you include a short video walkthrough of the rollback steps? That would help our SREs.
[00:09:38] Lena Park: Yes, we'll record a 7–10 minute walkthrough and share.
[00:09:42] Maya Singh: Thanks.
[00:09:44] Evan Cole: Thanks everyone, bye.
[00:09:46] Nora Patel: Bye.
[00:09:48] Sam Torres: Bye.
[00:09:50] Lena Park: Thanks, we'll follow up with notes and links. End meeting.

Notes/Artifacts referenced: rollout runbook doc (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link), security pack (link), sample harness container (link).

End of transcript.
